title: V'Zot HaBerachah: end with a blessing (Deuteronomy 33:1)
hookLine: Moses' last act is to bless each tribe

lines: AT THE BEDSIDE, AT THE GATE.
cards: Last words get said in ordinary places: at a hospital bedside, at an airport gate, at the end of a long phone call with someone far away. Some last words are instructions: take care of your mother.

Some are worries, some are apologies, and some are something else. The Torah's final portion opens with Moses' last words to the people. He has warned them, taught them, argued with them and sung to them.
Now he does one more thing.

teach.b: "And this is the blessing, wherewith Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel before his death." In Hebrew, v'zot haberachah: and this is the blessing. It's the one portion never read on an ordinary Shabbat.
It's read on Simchat Torah, the day the yearly cycle ends and begins again.
Notice the title Moses is given here: the man of God. After a lifetime of leading, his final role is to bless.
Then he goes tribe by tribe, the way his ancestor Jacob blessed his sons at the end of Genesis. Each tribe receives something different. For Judah, that its voice be heard.
For Levi, the work of teaching. For Zebulun, the riches of the sea. For Asher, a foot dipped in olive oil.
Not one blessing copied down the line. Each one fits. Rashi stops at the words before his death and reads them as close to his death.
If not now, when? There's no more time to wait. Moses has been angry with these people, disappointed by them, worn out by them.
He doesn't end with any of that. He ends with blessings, tribe by tribe, by name. This week walked from the hidden face to here.
Hidden, not gone. Heaven and earth listen. Drop as the rain.
The rock. Ask your elders. Spread the wings.
And now: end with a blessing.

how: V'Zot HaBerachah is read on Simchat Torah rather than on a Shabbat. On Friday nights it is a custom for parents to bless their children with the priestly blessing from Numbers 6.

games.q: you're Moses, worn out by these people after the long years in the wilderness, with one last chance to speak to them. what do you do?
o: list their failures, so they learn.
bless each tribe in its own way.
games.why: the Torah's last portion opens: and this is the blessing. Moses ends with fitted blessings, tribe by tribe.

practice: Think ahead to tonight: who will you see, or call, or think of?
There's a Jewish custom of parents blessing their children on Friday night with the old priestly words, "The LORD bless thee, and keep thee," and if you pray, you can use those words for someone.
If you don't, a specific wish will do, shaped to them, the way Moses shaped the tribes' blessings.
